subject: Intermittent response pile-up causing p99 spikes — update & exec brief
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@starlite-retail.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Pritchard <j.pritchard@starlite-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Aug 2029 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent long-tail latency and elevated error-rate - urgent

Hi Sofia / Jordan,

We started seeing recurring p99 spikes yesterday evening after the catalog personalization deploy (Aug 8, ~22:00 UTC). Notes so far:
- p95  stable (~180ms) but p99 jumps to 3.2s intermittently (every ~5–15 minutes for short windows)
- error-rate for generation endpoints increased from 0.2% -> 4.9% during spikes (timeout and 5xx)
- throughput drops observed concurrent with spikes (clients getting retries, effective RPS down ~20%)

This is impacting checkout personalization — we saw a few aborted carts and 502s in the logs. We've attached a small bundle of traces and sampled logs. Can your team confirm whether this looks like queueing/backpressure on your side or something in our integration? We have a big weekend promotion so need this stabilized ASAP.

Attachments: starlite-quicktraces-20290809.zip (zipped traces, sample span ids included in timeline)

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Engineering — Starlite Retail

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Aug 2029 19:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent long-tail latency and elevated error-rate - urgent

Team — quick triage notes after pairing with infra: 
1) Symptom summary: short windows of heavy p99 (2.5–3.5s) with associated error-rate blips and a drop in observed throughput on the affected model variant. Pattern looks like head-of-line blocking (one or a few long requests holding chunks of serving capacity), causing queue growth and client-side retries that amplify load.
2) Leads: 
   - Concurrency cap for Starlite's dedicated pool is at 64 concurrent requests per model shard; when rare long requests hit, remaining requests queue in front of GPU executor.
   - KV cache churn: high variability of prompt prefixes (personalization keys) is preventing reuse; KV cache misses increase per-token time for some requests leading to longer tails.
3) Immediate mitigations (applied now): 
   - Enabled request-timeout soft-fail at 2.2s for the most aggressive client route to trim runaway requests.
   - Briefly increased concurrency cap to 80 on one hot shard to test headroom.
   - Activated fallback routing to a slightly smaller quantized model for requests that exceed a 1.8s threshold (hoping to reduce GPU exec time).
4) Next steps (within 24h):
   - Collect canary metrics (p50/p95/p99, error-rate, queue length) and compare baseline; we uploaded canary logs.
   - If noise persists, propose a controlled pool-wide concurrency bump and KV cache warmup via a sampled prefix warming job.
   - Prepare an exec readout if we have customer-impacting errors for >6 hours.

Attachments: timeline.csv, canary-logs.txt

Marissa
Sr. Ops Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Update: short mitigation applied, monitoring ongoing

Hi Elena,

Quick update from our side after the mitigations Marissa described:
- We implemented the soft-fail and the per-request fallback; early canary metrics look promising — p99 reduced from ~3.2s to ~1.1–1.6s during the windows we reproduced.
- Error-rate is down to ~0.6% in the canary traffic slice; overall throughput dropped only minimally while we traded a small portion of requests to fallback model.
- We deployed a sampled prefix-warm job to reduce KV misses; it will run across business-hours for the next 48 hours.

Can we ask Starlite to keep production traffic monitoring on and flag any customer-facing anomalies? We'll send continuous updates and plan a 30m exec readout Monday morning to summarize root cause, actions, and any recommended commercial remediation.

Attachments: postpatch-metrics.png

Thanks for the quick coordination — we know the timing is unfortunate with your promotion.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2029 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec brief — Starlite long-tail latency incident & recommended commercial next steps

Leaders,

Summary (short): Starlite Retail experienced intermittent p99 spikes and a ~4–5% error-rate bump tied to head-of-line blocking and KV cache thrash after their Aug 8 personalization deploy. We implemented immediate mitigations (soft-fail, per-request fallback to a smaller quantized model, temporary concurrency increase on a hot shard, prefix warming). Early telemetry shows p99 improving to ~1.1–1.6s and error-rate normalizing (~0.6%).

Root cause (concise): A combination of tight concurrency caps + high variability of prompt prefixes produced cache miss amplification; long-running requests occasionally monopolized execution slots leading to queue growth.

Actions taken:
- Canary mitigations applied within 2 hours of first report; continuous monitoring for 72 hours.
- Live prefix-warm job to improve KV hit-rate over next 48h.
- Proposal: Increase committed concurrency for Starlite's dedicated pool by 25% (cost impact estimated in linked Jira) and provide a one-off service credit for errors during the incident window.

Customer ask: Starlite requested stability over the weekend and an exec-level readout. They may request credits if customer impact is validated.

Decision requested: Approve the temporary concurrency bump and the proposed service credit (recommendation: 15% of that week's hosted bill) so Sofia can close the loop and maintain the account health.

Links: Incident ticket RED-1198; canary metrics folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-starlite-incident

Jordan Blake
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
